results.title: UPDATE: Reports from Mada, Gusau LGA of Zamfara State, suggest that more than 40 bandits have been killed in the ongoing clash between rival
results.description:
UPDATE: Reports from Mada, Gusau LGA of Zamfara State, suggest that more than 40 bandits have been killed in the ongoing clash between rival groups. Those reportedly killed include Kachallah Dogo Baldu and Sanata, the younger brother of Ado Aleru.

This development could bring some relief to residents who have suffered years of bandit attacks, kidnappings and cattle rustling. For the people of Zamfara, this is a welcome development, and everyone hopes it will translate into lasting peace and safety for their communities.

results.title: Notorious bandit leader Muhammad Gwaska has displaced residents of Birnin Doki in the troubled Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State a
results.description:
Notorious bandit leader Muhammad Gwaska has displaced residents of Birnin Doki in the troubled Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State after they resisted pressure to work at mining sites under his control.

The incident, which occurred on 15 October, saw dozens of villagers forced to walk about a 15-kilometre distance from Birnin Doki to the local government headquarters in Anka town. Since their arrival, local government authorities have shown them an abandoned and dilapidated structure that used to be a veterinary clinic to camp in.

results.title: UPDATE: The bandits who invaded Birnin Tudu community in Gummi LGA, Zamfara State, have been chased away by local vigilantes.
results.description:
UPDATE: The bandits who invaded Birnin Tudu community in Gummi LGA, Zamfara State, have been chased away by local vigilantes.

Thankfully, no one was killed, injured or abducted, and no livestock was looted or rustled before the bandits fled.

Kudos to the vigilantes for standing up to the attackers and protecting their community. Their bravery and quick response deserve to be commended

Bandit leader expels Zamfara community for refusing to mine for him

Authorities in Zamfara, like other parts of northern Nigeria, have become numb to what is happening to their people. How can an entire community be expelled by a bandit leader and local authorities turn a blind eye, pretending not to be aware?

No adequate shelter, no food, no acknowledgement of their condition. NOTHING. It's a crazy experience for people down there.
